summary: Reviewed 3 files (tool_wrappers.py, nodes/__init__.py, test_tool_wrappers.py). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (design edge case — noted), 1 Low (observability). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Medium — A04 Insecure Design (edge case, not exploitable in current usage). File: orchestrator/src/utils/tool_wrappers.py — restrict_to_wp(). The sentinel pattern (_orig_ainvoke_wp) stores the first-time original ainvoke; subsequent wraps always delegate directly to that original, bypassing any earlier wrap. In the standard pipeline each tool instance is only ever wrapped with one WP ID, so this is benign. However, if a future refactor shares tool instances across concurrent pipeline stages with different wp_ids, only the last guard's closure would be active — the previous guards would be silently bypassed when the sentinel short-circuits. This is a latent design risk. Recommendation: document the single-WP-per-tool-instance invariant in tool_wrappers.py, or gate the sentinel on (sentinel_wp_id == wp_id) instead of just hasattr.

Low — A09 Security Logging & Monitoring. File: orchestrator/src/utils/tool_wrappers.py — _guarded_ainvoke(). The ValueError rejection path is silent: no log entry records that a cross-WP call was blocked. In a headless pipeline run this event is only visible if the exception propagates to the run logger upstream. Recommendation: add a log.warning() call before raising ValueError so security-relevant rejections are captured in the structured JSONL run log regardless of exception handling upstream.

No other security findings. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed: A01 (access control guard is correctly applied — inject when absent, reject on explicit mismatch), A02 (no crypto), A03 (no injection — wp_id interpolation via .format() uses trusted internal ledger data constrained to WP-NNN pattern), A04 (see Medium note), A05 (no config exposure), A06 (no new dependencies), A07 (no auth), A08 (no deserialization), A09 (see Low note), A10 (no SSRF). OWASP review complete.

summary: Reviewed WP-003: Cross-WP tool guard hardening in orchestrator/src/utils/tool_wrappers.py and orchestrator/src/nodes/__init__.py.

restrict_to_wp(): injection path (absent wp_id → inject active WP) and rejection path (explicit wrong wp_id → ValueError) are both correct. Handles flat-dict and ToolCall structures via the same pattern as inject_project_path. Idempotency sentinel prevents closure stacking. Empty wp_id guard correctly bypasses synthesis stages.

_WP_SCOPE_REMINDER: module-level constant using lazy .format(wp_id=wp_id) is the correct pattern for a module-level string template. build_stage_prompt() guard on 'if wp_id:' ensures the CRITICAL reminder only appears in WP-scoped stages.
Tests cover: injection (flat-dict), injection (ToolCall), rejection (flat-dict), rejection (ToolCall), matching WP passthrough, non-dict passthrough, idempotency, empty-wp_id skip. Comprehensive.
Security Auditor's medium finding (sentinel single-WP invariant) and low finding (silent rejection) both endorsed. Neither blocks PASS. Both documented as improvement comments.
AC2 and AC5 are semantically identical — noted as convention observation for future WP planning.

comments.note: Endorsing the Security Auditor's medium finding (sentinel double-wrap latent risk): add a docstring or inline comment in restrict_to_wp() explicitly documenting the invariant 'tool instances must not be shared across concurrent pipeline stages with different wp_ids'. This is the minimal fix. The stronger fix (gating sentinel on sentinel_wp_id == wp_id) would be safer but is a behavioral change that should go back to Developer if desired.

Endorsing the Security Auditor's low finding: the ValueError rejection path in _guarded_ainvoke() should emit a log.warning() before raising. This makes cross-WP rejection events visible in the structured JSONL run log without requiring the caller to catch and log the exception. Example: log.warning('Cross-WP tool call blocked: call_wp_id=%r, active_wp_id=%r, tool=%s', call_wp_id, _active_wp, getattr(_orig, '__self__', {}).name if hasattr(_orig, '__self__') else '')

AC2 and AC5 are semantically identical ('Tool calls with explicitly wrong work_package_id are still rejected' vs. 'Tool calls with explicitly wrong work_package_id are still rejected with ValueError'). Future WP planning should avoid duplicate acceptance criteria; they waste review time and can cause confusing 'unmet' states when only one is updated.
